narrative.overview:
StreamLine's visual system is a reference-grade tool — like a calibrated studio monitor used by audio engineers. What you see is project reality without filter or enhancement. The interface does not celebrate itself. It is dark so that the work is visible; it is quiet so that signals are heard; it is dense because professionals need information, not whitespace.

Clean and professional — the kind of tool you show a client during a call without hesitation. Every design decision asks: does this make the information clearer, or does it add visual noise?

This system explicitly rejects the generic purple SaaS scaffold and the playful startup aesthetic. Studio Violet exists to mark a single thing at a time: the one action worth taking, the one status that needs attention. Its rarity is the point.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal depth replaces shadow — four surface layers create hierarchy without blur
Studio Violet appears on ≤15% of any screen, always earning its presence
Inter at tight tracking creates a precise, focused reading environment
Semantic color is never decorative — success green and warning amber mean exactly that
Motion is exponential-ease under 350ms; never decorative choreography

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Studio Violet marks a single thing at a time: the primary CTA or the active state. Two violet elements on the same screen compete and collapse into decoration.

rules.name: The Semantic Lock
rules.body: Signal Green means active or approved. Signal Amber means attention needed. Signal Red means error or destructive. These colors never appear for decorative or brand purposes.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked label type is reserved for table column headers only — not for stat card categories or section eyebrows. If every section has an uppercase label, none of them carry weight.

rules.name: The Tight Tracking Floor
rules.body: Display headings use letter-spacing -0.02em minimum. Labels use 0.06em maximum. The gap between these poles creates the typographic rhythm.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are always flat at rest. No box-shadow on cards, no backdrop-filter on overlays, no frosted glass. Tonal color is the depth system.

rules.name: The Modal Exception
rules.body: The single allowed shadow is on modal/dialog overlays: 0 25px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.5). This is structural, not decorative.

dos: Use Studio Violet exclusively for the single primary CTA, active nav state background, and critical status indicators — one per context at most
Use border-radius 8px on buttons and inputs, 12px on cards and panels
Use semantic color with 15% opacity backgrounds for badges: green for approved/active, amber for pending/warning, red for errors
Use exponential easing (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for entrances and state transitions, 150–350ms duration
Include prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks on all Framer Motion animations
Test every Ink Muted text value against its actual surface for 4.5:1 contrast
Use text-wrap: balance on all h1–h3 headings
donts: Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent on navigation items, cards, or callouts — this is a banned pattern
Don't use uppercase tracked label text above stat cards, section headings, or dashboard panels as eyebrow decorations
Don't use Studio Violet as a fill color on more than one primary action per screen
Don't add gradient text, glassmorphism cards, or backdrop-filter blur effects — flat by doctrine
Don't build identical card grids with same icon, heading, body, size repeated four or more times
Don't use Studio Violet as a background fill on any surface other than the primary button and the notification badge
Don't ship placeholder or hardcoded user data in production views
Don't add box-shadow to cards or any UI component except the single permitted modal overlay shadow
